vectors.description: REQUEST_OK with no parameters and empty Track Properties. Section 9.3: it answers PUBLISH, FETCH, REQUEST_UPDATE, TRACK_STATUS, SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS and PUBLISH_NAMESPACE
REQUEST_OK with LARGEST_OBJECT parameter (group=10, object=3) — typically a REQUEST_UPDATE_OK
REQUEST_UPDATE_OK carrying EXPIRES (60000ms) and LARGEST_OBJECT (group=10, object=3); demonstrates type-delta ordering (0x08 then a delta of 1 to 0x09)
TRACK_STATUS_OK (REQUEST_OK in response to TRACK_STATUS) with LARGEST_OBJECT param and track properties

TRACK_STATUS_OK carrying EXPIRES (30000ms) and LARGEST_OBJECT {5,0}. Section 9.3 lists "TRACK_STATUS_OK: EXPIRES, LARGEST_OBJECT"; draft-22 allowed LARGEST_OBJECT alone there. Section 9.19.16: "EXPIRES in TRACK_STATUS_OK indicates the value the sender would have included in a SUBSCRIBE_OK for the same Track."

FETCH_OK with LARGEST_OBJECT {5,3}. Draft-23 removed the FETCH_OK message (0x18) and answers FETCH with REQUEST_OK; Section 1.5 keeps FETCH_OK as the name of that REQUEST_OK. Section 3.2: "If Largest Object is within the requested range, the FETCH response ends at Largest Object and the publisher MUST include the LARGEST_OBJECT parameter (Section 9.19.17) in FETCH_OK."

FETCH_OK with no parameters and Track Properties OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT=5000ms and DYNAMIC_GROUPS=1. Without LARGEST_OBJECT the response ends at the requested End Location (Section 3.2). Section 9.3: "Track Properties are populated in TRACK_STATUS_OK and FETCH_OK"

FETCH_OK carrying EXPIRES (30ms) and LARGEST_OBJECT {10,3}, with Track Property OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT=5000ms. Section 9.3 lists "FETCH_OK: EXPIRES, LARGEST_OBJECT". Draft-22's FETCH_OK could carry neither parameter

non-canonical REQUEST_OK — same parameters as with-expires-and-largest-object, but the LARGEST_OBJECT parameter type delta (value 1) is encoded as a 2-byte varint (8001) instead of the canonical 1-byte form (01); decoders MUST accept

non-canonical REQUEST_OK — same parameters as with-expires-and-largest-object, but the LARGEST_OBJECT parameter type delta (value 1) is encoded as a 4-byte varint (e0000001) instead of the canonical 1-byte form (01); decoders MUST accept

non-canonical REQUEST_OK — same parameters as with-expires-and-largest-object, but the LARGEST_OBJECT parameter type delta (value 1) is encoded as a 8-byte varint (fe00000000000001) instead of the canonical 1-byte form (01); decoders MUST accept

non-canonical REQUEST_OK — the minimal REQUEST_OK with its Message Length (1) written as the 2-byte vi64 8001. The Length is a vi64 (Section 9, Figure 6), so a non-minimal form is valid (Section 8.1). Decode-only

non-canonical REQUEST_OK — the minimal REQUEST_OK with its Message Length (1) written as the 3-byte vi64 c00001. The Length is a vi64 (Section 9, Figure 6), so a non-minimal form is valid (Section 8.1). Decode-only

REQUEST_OK whose Message Length is 0. The frame is complete and its body lacks the Number of Parameters. Section 9: "If the length does not match the length of the Message Body, the receiver MUST close the session with MALFORMED_MESSAGE." The two bytes are the start of draft-22's minimal REQUEST_OK, 07 00 01 00, whose Length was 16 bits
vectors.error_detail: Length 0 leaves no Number of Parameters
unexpected end of input while reading parameter count
